verdict.rationale: Obsidian's docs say notes are stored locally as non-proprietary plain-text Markdown files, giving users total control so they can 'switch to another app easily'. Because the vault is already in an open format, the whole knowledge base can be taken away at any time. Community users corroborate this: they describe files that outlive the app, file ownership, and a future-proof format, and they note Canvas uses an MIT-licensed open JSON format. Missing for 10: no evidence on how portable Obsidian-specific syntax (internal links, Bases views) is in other apps, and some concern that Canvas JSON is less readable than Markdown.
